title: EPA plans PFAS rule rollbacks that loom large in W.Va. after court tosses Chemours order
description: The United States Environmental Protection Agency under President Donald Trump has proposed to eliminate maximum contamination levels and the country’s first ever national drinking water limits implemented for certain PFAS, targeting measures enacted in 2024 under then-President Joe Biden. Trump's EPA is proposing to allow for a two-year extension of compliance deadlines set under Biden in 2024 for two of the most common PFAS, PFOA and PFOS. The EPA also has proposed rescinding legally enforceable maximum contamination levels set in 2024 for three PFAS known as HFPO-DA, PFHxS (perfluorohexane sulfonic acid) and PFNA (perfluorononanoic acid), as well as mixtures of those PFAS plus another known as PFBS (perfluorobutane sulfonic acid). The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit tossed a preliminary injunction approved by the District Court for the Southern District of West Virginia in a June 3, 2026 ruling, siding with Chemours after it argued the district court erred in finding “irreparable harm” from the company’s Washington Works plant polluting a PFAS known as HFPO-DA (hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid) or GenX chemicals.
